patch.objective: In a COPD exacerbation, titrate oxygen and follow blood gases for CO2 retention, recognizing pursed-lip breathing and tripod positioning as cues of distress
secondaryObjectives: Acute respiratory failure: recognizing it and escalating support in time

sources.cite: Davidson AC, Banham S, Elliott M, et al. BTS/ICS guideline for the ventilatory management of acute hypercapnic respiratory failure in adults. Thorax 2016;71(Suppl 2):ii1-ii35
sources.note: Relayed from the PCCN case copd-exacerbation-niv, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-14 through a summarizing fetch (approved for publication November 2015; no newer BTS/ICS version was found). Controlled oxygen to SpO2 88-92% in AECOPD (Grade A); NIV when pH <7.35 and PaCO2 >6.5 kPa (about 49 mm Hg) persist or develop despite optimal medical therapy (Grade A), in practice after about 60 minutes with RR >23; start IPAP about 15 and raise it to 20-30 cm H2O within 10-30 minutes, EPAP at least 3; ABG before and after starting NIV; worsening pH and respiratory rate mean the strategy must change, and invasive ventilation should be considered for persistent or worsening acidosis despite optimized NIV (Grade A); pH <7.25 with RR >35 that persists makes NIV failure likely; care plans should include escalation arrangements from the start.
